chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin'an, who said:

A believer was mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Indeed, the believer is the one who, when angered, his anger does not lead him away from the truth; and the believer is the one who, when pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into falsehood; and the believer is the one who, when in power, does not acquire what does not belong to him [by himself].'
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of a perfect believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to define the 'perfect believer' (al-Mu’min al-Kamil) through emotional and ethical stability. The Imam emphasizes that true faith requires maintaining justice and truth during anger, avoiding bias in pleasure, and exercising restraint in power, reflecting the Shia concept of *‘adl* (justice) as an internal state before external action. This triad highlights the believer's mastery over their *nafs* (self) to prevent passions from distorting their judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-67 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Safvan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an,

“A believer’s name was mentioned to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB). The Imam (MGB) said, ‘Indeed a believer is one who when angered, his anger would not lead him away from the right. A believer is one who when pleased, his pleasure would not lead him into the wrong. A believer is one who when in power, his power would not lead him to acquire what doesn’t rightfully belong to him.’”
